recipes.title: BREAD PUDDING
recipes.description: A 1930 recipe featuring 2 cups stale bread crumbs, 2 eggs, and 1 qt. scalded milk.
steps: Soak bread crumbs in milk. When cool add sugar, slightly beaten eggs, salt and flavoring. Bake in moderate oven about 1 hour or until set and firm.
**Variations:**
1. Use brown sugar.
2. Caramelize 1/3 cup sugar, add milk and scald. When smooth proceed as given.
3. Melt 2 squares of chocolate. Add milk and scald.
4. Add 1/2 cup raisins and 1/2 cup currants.
5. Save one egg white. When pudding is baked spread with jelly and meringue and brown.

steps: To the sugar add water and 1/4 tsp. cream of tartar. Stir until sugar is dissolved, and boil until a little tried in cold water forms a firm ball ( 250 ° F. ). While the syrup is cooking beat the egg whites until stiff and dry, adding the salt before beating. Pour the syrup slowly on to the whites, beating constantly, and beat until cool. Add vanilla. Fold in the flour, which has been sifted several times with the remainder of the cream of tartar. Turn into an ungreased tube pan, place in a cold oven, and raise temperature gradually to 300°. Time in combining, 30 minutes; time in cooking, 1 hour 10 minutes. Temperature, 300°. Recipe makes loaf in tube pan 8 inches in diameter.

recipes.title: GOLD MEDAL CAKE
recipes.description: A 1930 recipe featuring ½ cup shortening, 1 tsp. flavoring, and 1 cup sugar.
steps: **Method:**
1. Cream shortening and sugar together.
2. Add the yolks, which have been beaten until light, with the water and flavoring.
3. Mix well.
4. Sift the dry ingredients together, and add to the first mix-ture alternately with the milk.
5. Fold in the beaten egg whites to which the salt has been added before beating.

6. May be baked as a loaf cake or in two layers. Time: Bake 40 minutes for loaf cake, 20 minutes for layer cake. Temperature: 325° F. for loaf cake and 375° for layer cake. Size of pan: Layer pans 9 inch diameter, oblong pan 9x16 in. Amount: 16 servings.

recipes.title: CHOCOLATE ORANGE CREAM WAFERS
recipes.description: A 1930 recipe featuring ¼ lb. bitter chocolate, ¼ lb. sweet chocolate, and 1¼ cups confectioners' sugar.
ingredient_search_terms: 3 4 cup finely cut crystallized orange peel
ingredients: 3/4 cup finely cut crystallized orange peel
steps: Melt the bitter chocolate in a double boiler and spread with a knife on heavy waxed paper on which has been drawn an oblong six inches by twelve inches. To the confectioners sugar add one teaspoon grated orange peel and two tablespoons juice ( enough to moisten the sugar so that it will spread without running). Add the crystallized orange peel and when the oblong of chocolate is hard spread on it the orange mixture as evenly as possible. Melt the sweet chocolate and spread on another sheet of waxed paper, making an oblong the same size as the first. Turn the first sheet face

down on this melted chocolate and press with the hand over the wrong side of the paper. When the chocolate is hard pull off the papers and cut the candy in squares to serve as a confection. This is really a very simple process, and the wafers are delicious, something one cannot buy at any candy shop.

recipes.title: STRAWBERRY MERINGUE
recipes.description: A 1930 recipe featuring 3 cups stale bread- crumbs, Grated rind half a lemon, and 1 qt. milk.
steps: Time: Preparation and baking, 30 minutes at 350°. 20 minutes at 335 °. Number served: 6 to 8 persons.
**Method:**

Soak bread crumbs in milk; when soft, add sugar, salt, beaten yolks, lemon rind, butter; mix. Pour into a shallow greased dish, and bake in a moderate oven until set about thirty minutes. When done, cover the top with berries, sweetened as necessary, and heap with stiff meringue made from the whites of eggs and powdered sugar. Brown in moderate oven. Serve cold. The pudding may be made several hours before serving, but the berries and meringue should both be added shortly before serving. Jam may be substituted for berries.

recipes.title: PINEAPPLE PIE
recipes.description: A 1930 recipe featuring Plain or puff paste, 2 eggs, and 1 ripe pineapple.
steps: Time: Preparation and baking. Bake 30 minutes 400°. Bake meringue 15 minutes 325°.
**Method:**

Pare pineapple, chop fine. Measure three cupfuls. Add sugar, cook until tender, about thirty minutes. Add flour moistened with water cook five minutes. Remove from fire, add yolks and salt. Line a pie-plate with a well-made paste, rolled thin. Pour in the pineapple, bake in a hot oven thirty minutes. Beat whites until stiff,

adding pinch of salt; add powdered sugar gradually. Heap meringue on top of pie, sprinkle with sugar, brown in moderate oven. Serve cool. For a flaky paste, allow one-third cupful shortening to threefourths cupful flour. Work one-half into flour, moisten with ice water, pat, roll out; fold in remainder, pat, roll; repeat.

recipes.title: SPANISH STEAK
recipes.description: A 1930 recipe featuring Steak, cut 1½ inches thick, ½ cup water, and Onions, thinly sliced.
steps: Steak cut 1½ inches thick, sear on both sides in hot frying pan. Put it in a casserole with 1/2 cup water and cover with thinly sliced onions. Cover the casserole and bake 30 minutes at 400 degrees, or less. Season with salt, pepper and pour 3 cups strained tomatoes over the meat. Bake about 40 minutes longer, uncovered. Place meat on platter, cover with grated cheese, and return to oven just long enough to melt cheese. Serve any gravy left in casserole right on platter with meat.

steps: Currant Jelly Place a 10 to 12 pound Swift's Premium Ham, fat side up, in an uncovered baking pan, in a 300 ° F. oven, allowing about 20 minutes per pound. steps: Beat egg slightly with salt and water. Add flour, cutting mixture with a knife. Knead until smooth and stiff. One or two more tbsp. flour may be necessary. Roll on a slightly floured molding board until as thin as possible. Cover and let stand 20 minutes. Cut in tiny squares, and let dry for 30 minutes. recipes.title: ROAST TURKEY AND DRESSING
recipes.description: A 1930 recipe featuring 1 turkey, about 12–14 lb, 8–10 cups dry bread cubes for dressing, and 1 small onion, minced.
ingredient_search_terms: 810 cups dry bread cubes for dressing
butter or bacon fat for rubbing bird
sage parsley salt and pepper to taste
stock or water as needed to moisten dressing
water or stock for pan and gravy
ingredients: 8–10 cups dry bread cubes for dressing
Sage, parsley, salt and pepper, to taste
Stock or water, as needed to moisten dressing
Butter or bacon fat, for rubbing bird
Water or stock, for pan and gravy
steps: Heat oven to 325°F. Remove giblets and pat the turkey dry. For dressing, toss bread cubes with sautéed onion and celery, melted butter, sage, parsley, salt and pepper; moisten lightly with stock. Bake the dressing separately in a buttered dish at 350°F for 30–40 minutes, until heated through and browned.

Season the turkey with salt and pepper and rub with butter or bacon fat. Place on a rack in a roasting pan with a little water or stock. Roast at 325°F, basting occasionally, until the thickest part of breast registers 165°F and the thigh is cooked through (roughly 3–4 hours for a 12–14 lb. unstuffed bird; check early). Rest 20–30 minutes before carving.

For gravy, simmer giblets separately if using. Skim fat from pan juices, whisk flour into a few tablespoons of fat, and add pan juices and stock until the desired thickness is reached. Season to taste.

steps: Use a shallow baking dish ( about 1/2 inches deep). Put a little melted butter in the bottom, and a layer of crushed (not pulverized ) crackers, then a layer of oysters. Season with salt and paprika, and pour over this cream. Add crackers, lumps of butter, oysters, and seasoning, until the dish is full. Over the last layer of crackers pour cream enough to moisten. steps: Soak 2 qts. navy beans overnight. Wash and drain. Cover with boiling water; at the boil add 2 large tsp. soda and boil a few minutes. Drain, add fresh water, and boil until skins curl.
If desired, reserve about 1½ cups beans for soup in some cooking water with a small piece of salt pork, seasoning, and onion. Boil soup about 2 hours, adding water as needed.

Layer bacon, onion, and beans in a large crock, burying 1½ lb. salt pork (part lean) just below the surface. Combine boiling water, mustard, catsup, molasses, oyster cocktail sauce, salt, and pepper. Pour over beans. Add reserved sauce as needed. Bake about six hours at 325°F. Serves 25.

recipes.title: POTATOES, EGG TIMBALES
recipes.description: A 1930 recipe featuring 2 cups cold boiled potatoes, 2 level tbsp. butter, or other fat, and chopped.
ingredient_search_terms: 2 level tbsp butter or other fat
ingredients: 2 level tbsp. butter, or other fat
steps: Time: Preparation and cooking, 30 minutes. Number served: 4 persons. Season the potatoes, sprinkle with flour, add milk, mix lightly. Put the butter into a saucepan; when melted and hot (not brown) put in the potatoes; pack down lightly, cook until deep brown on bottom; fold over as you would an omelet, cook five minutes longer, turn out carefully on a hot platter. While potatoes are browning prepare eggs. Grease small molds or cups, cover inside with parsley and ham; break an egg into each. Stand in a pan half full of water; cook slowly-on top of stove, or in oven-until eggs are set. Turn out on potatoes.

recipes.title: STUFFED ONIONS
recipes.description: A 1930 recipe featuring 6 large Bermuda onions, 1 cup chopped nutmeats, and 1 cup fine dried bread crumbs.
steps: Peel onions and cook in boiling salted water for 45 minutes. Cool, cut a slice from the top of each and scoop out the centers, leaving a shell about ¾ inch thick. Combine nutmeats, bread crumbs, butter, salt, pepper and parsley; fill onion shells. Put in a buttered baking dish, add 1 cup boiling water and bake 20 minutes. Baste with 1 tbsp. butter melted in a little hot water.

For the sauce, melt 2 tbsp. butter, stir in flour and cook, stirring constantly until blended and bubbly. Slowly add milk and bring to a boil. Stir in cheese until melted; remove from heat and beat in egg yolk. Do not boil after cheese and yolk are added. Serve stuffed onions surrounded by sauce.

recipes.title: CREAM OF MUSHROOM SOUP
recipes.description: A 1930 recipe featuring 1 qt. thin white sauce, 1 can mushrooms, cut up.
steps: Prepare 1 quart of thin white sauce (about 2 tbsp. butter, 2 tbsp. flour and 4 cups milk, cooked until lightly thickened). Drain and chop mushrooms, reserving a little of their liquid if desired. Stir mushrooms into the white sauce, simmer gently 5–10 minutes and season with salt and pepper. Thin with milk or mushroom liquid to serving consistency.

recipes.title: CREAM OF ONION SOUP
recipes.description: A 1930 recipe featuring 1 cup thinly sliced onions, 2½ cups milk, and 2 tbsp. butter.
steps: Melt butter and fat in pan without letting the fats bubble, add onion slices and cook over a low fire 30 minutes. Keep the pan closely covered, letting the onions cook in their own juice and steam. When the onions are soft add flour and stir with a fork until thoroughly blended. Add milk, salt and pepper and bring to the boiling point, stirring constantly. Let boil 5 minutes, and rub through a strainer. Add egg slightly beaten and reheat over hot water if necessary. Whip cream and serve a spoonful sprinkled with parsley on each portion.

recipes.title: Providence Muffins
recipes.description: A 1930 recipe featuring ½ cup graham flour, ½ cup bran, and ½ teaspoon salt.

recipes.title: Mahogany Cake
recipes.description: A 1930 recipe featuring Chocolate mixture: ½ cup milk, Chocolate mixture: ½ cup cocoa, and ½ cup butter.
steps: Cook the first ½ cup milk with cocoa until thick and smooth; cool. Cream butter and sugar, then add beaten egg yolks. Sift together flour, baking soda, and baking powder, and add alternately with milk. Add cooled chocolate mixture and vanilla. Fold in stiffly beaten egg whites. Bake in two greased nine-inch layer pans at 350°F for about 30 minutes. Spread Fudge Frosting between layers and over the cake.

recipes.title: Fudge Frosting
recipes.description: A 1930 recipe featuring 2 cups sugar, 3 squares (3 oz.) unsweetened chocolate, and 2 tablespoons corn syrup.
steps: Cook sugar, chocolate, corn syrup, and milk, stirring until sugar dissolves. Stir occasionally to prevent burning. Cook to 232°F or to the very-soft-ball stage. Remove from heat and add baking powder and butter. Cool to lukewarm, add vanilla, and beat until creamy and spreadable.

recipes.description: A 1930 recipe featuring 1 slice Swift’s Premium Savor-tite ham, about ½ inch thick, Brookfield butter, for browning, and Mushrooms, fresh or canned.

steps: Brown one side of ham in butter. Turn so the browned side faces up. Cover with mushrooms, cover the pan and simmer about 15 minutes, or until mushrooms are tender. Serve on a platter with sliced pineapple. If using canned mushrooms, reserve their liquid for gravy.
